title: Commentary: fire at Episil threatens tight epitaxial wafer supply
content: A fire broke out at the Innovation Plant of semiconductor epitaxial wafer maker Episil on October 28. The extent of equipment damage, the scope of production stoppages, and the recovery timeline remain under clarification. With certain products from Episil already experiencing tight supply, largely driven by wafer manufacturing customers lacking internal adjustable capacity, any damage to existing mass-production equipment risks widening the current supply gap.

title: UMT reports 71% revenue growth as LEO satellite demand drives expansion
content: UMT's revenue increased 71% year-over-year in the first three quarters of 2026 as global demand for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite deployments lifted sales of millimeter-wave communications products. The Taiwan-based company said it would begin advancing manufacturing expansion plans in Taiwan, the US, and Vietnam from the fourth quarter of 2026 to support international customer demand and strengthen delivery flexibility.

title: TSMC buys AUO Taichung plant for NT$38.8B; Quanta deal scrapped
content: AUO has approved the sale of its Taichung Plant Phase II facilities and related infrastructure to TSMC for NT$38.8 billion (US$1.2 billion), excluding taxes, and has terminated a planned NT$19.7 billion sale of its Huaya facilities to Quanta after the two companies failed to agree on usage specifications and delivery schedules. AUO expects the Taichung transaction to generate approximately NT$18.5 billion in disposal gains after related transaction costs and estimated taxes.

title: Analysis: Samsung's record quarter came from higher prices, not more chips; expects buyers to get no relief before 2028
content: Samsung Electronics' third-quarter profit came almost entirely from charging more for memory chips, not from selling more of them. On its earnings call, the company also told investors the shortage behind those prices will last into 2028, even as chipmakers raise spending.

title: Server CPU shipments set to surge 46% in 2027, with AMD eyeing revenue crown
content: Global server CPU shipments are projected to surpass the 50 million-unit milestone for the first time in 2027, reaching 52.6 million units as demand accelerates alongside the industry-wide shift from AI training to inference, according to DIGITIMES Intelligence. While Intel is expected to retain its shipment crown, rival AMD is closing in fast.

title: Marvell reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum in AI optics deal
content: Marvell Technology is in advanced talks to acquire data-center optical component maker Lumentum Holdings, people familiar with the matter said, in what could become a major AI hardware supply-chain deal. The transaction could be announced as early as next week.

title: Nvidia under probe by US justice officials over Hugging Face acquisition
content: The US Department of Justice (DOJ) is reviewing how Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face could affect competition in the AI industry, while a years-long antitrust investigation continues into the company's broader practices. The probes target a chipmaker that has grown into the world's biggest company by market capitalization, with business interests spanning multiple parts of the AI value chain, and is a major backer of data center development.

title: LB Semicon to expand PMIC capacity under 10-year Qualcomm deal

title: KLA: wafer fab equipment market exceeding US$200B in 2027
content: KLA expects global wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending to exceed US$200 billion in 2027, as semiconductor manufacturers accelerate investments in advanced logic, DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), according to executives on the company's October 28 earnings call. The projection marks an improvement over its outlook for the current year and reflects growing confidence in a prolonged semiconductor investment cycle.

title: SDC chief meets Applied Materials executives amid FMM-free OLED push
content: Samsung Display (SDC) President Lee Chung-hwan recently met with senior executives from US equipment maker Applied Materials as SDC accelerates development of fine metal mask (FMM)-free OLED technology. The meeting has drawn attention as SDC and Chinese panel maker Visionox compete to advance FMM-free technologies such as MPO and ViP, along with the related equipment infrastructure.

title: NXP wins Volkswagen role in software-defined vehicle architecture
content: Volkswagen Group and NXP Semiconductors have agreed on a strategic partnership under which NXP's S32K5 microcontrollers (MCUs) are intended to serve as a building block of the carmaker's future software-defined vehicle architecture.

title: Kuen Tong debuts on TPEx Emerging Board, riding LEO satellite and AI cooling dual engines
content: Taiwan's Kuen Tong Technology, a high-end precision metal components maker and major supplier to a US low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operator, is set to list on the Taipei Exchange's Emerging Stock Board on October 29 at a reference price of NT$390 (approx. US$12.03) per share. Riding rising satellite demand, the company plans to expand production capacity in Thailand from 2027 while developing AI server liquid cooling and semiconductor equipment businesses.

title: CyberLink blasts Apple over developer account suspension
content: CyberLink faces mounting pressure from rising memory prices and removal of some of its products from Apple's platform, with the multimedia software provider warning that restoring its developer account could take up to a year. CyberLink chairman Jau Huang criticized Apple for what he called heavy-handed handling of small software developers.

title: UMC targets 10% ASP growth in 2027 as AI revenue share heads toward 25% within three years
content: United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) expects wafer foundry pricing to continue rising in 2027, with CEO Jason Wang projecting approximately 10% year-over-year growth in the company's full-year average selling price (ASP).

title: CXMT to start HBM3E production despite low yields amid tight domestic market
content: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's leading producer of DRAM memory, is reportedly planning to begin production of HBM3E, despite yields so far only reaching 20% to 30%. This reflects the memory shortage faced by China's market as it seeks to expand its domestic capacity while facing restrictions on critical equipment imports.
